_README: Label id -> structure name for the upper-limb muscle COMPARTMENT volume derived from the Visible Human male colour cryosections by scripts/cryo/arm_compartments_from_cryo.py, plus the mapping onto atlas entities.

A KEY, not data. The arm's muscle mass (muscle-coloured pixels connected to the humerus, between the elbow joint line and 70 mm below the humeral head) is split by the coronal plane through the humerus centre: anterior = flexor compartment (biceps brachii, brachialis, coracobrachialis), posterior = extensor compartment (triceps brachii). The intermuscular septa are oblique to that plane, so the boundary is approximate; nothing here separates individual muscles. The forearm labels (3,4,7,8) are NOT mapped: the arm lies pronated against the thigh and an image-frame anterior/posterior split does not follow the flexor/extensor septa.
source: U.S. National Library of Medicine, The Visible Human Project (public domain), male colour cryosections, IDC series 4aaf9181-fb6a-4a4c-bf49-d1eb9ed4a385, registered to the CT (scripts/cryo/README.md). Compartment membership: Standring S (ed.), Gray's Anatomy, 42nd ed., Elsevier 2021, ch. 'Elbow and forearm' / 'Shoulder girdle and arm' (fascial compartments of the arm).
